mitigation_descriptions: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow and sensitive credential stores are properly restricted to prevent unauthorized read access.
Audit and configure sudoers files to prevent non-administrative users from executing binaries like /bin/cat against sensitive system files.
Manage and audit privileged accounts and sudo privileges to ensure adherence to the principle of least privilege.
Enforce password rotation and complexity requirements for accounts whose hashes may have been exposed.
reasoning: The adversary successfully executed a privileged command to dump password hashes from /etc/shadow using account gmorgan on intranet-server, confirming technique T1003.008. Immediate containment and credential rotation are necessary to prevent offline cracking and lateral movement.
remediation_plan: 1. Isolate the affected host intranet-server (192.168.104.155) from the network to prevent further lateral movement. 2. Suspend or revoke active sessions and credentials for the compromised user account gmorgan. 3. Initiate an immediate password reset for all local user and service accounts present on intranet-server whose hashes were exposed via /etc/shadow. 4. Review and restrict the /etc/sudoers configuration on intranet-server to revoke unauthorized sudo privileges for /bin/cat and other file viewing binaries. 5. Verify and restore appropriate file permissions and ownership on /etc/shadow (e.g., chmod 000 /etc/shadow or 640 root:shadow). 6. Inspect authentication and command-line execution logs for any additional anomalous activities originating from agent ID 26.
